playbook:
**Playbook for ref_commons**

- When the game is a shared renewable stock with a fixed number of seasons, my default each season is the announced sustainable share per boat. It keeps the stock at cap and pays out every round. Matching it exactly worked for five straight seasons in practice.

- Watch the other boats' reported catches each season. If everyone is at the sustainable share and the stock holds steady, keep matching it exactly. Cooperation is stable and profitable; don't be the first to defect while many seasons remain.

- If one boat overfishes but the stock stays well above zero, I do not need to retaliate immediately. A single defection (boat 1 took 15.0 in season 5) cost me little and cooperation otherwise held. Retaliation only makes sense if it prevents future overfishing with enough seasons left to matter.

- In the FINAL season, conservation value is zero — take everything the stock can support. I took the whole remaining stock (94.2) in season 6 and it worked: no penalty, maximum payoff. Don't take a token amount above sustainable; take it all.

- Before submitting a final-season grab, check whether the stock is large enough that one boat can't take it all or whether catches are capped. If there's an explicit maximum or a per-boat limit, take that maximum. If others might race me to it, still grab the largest amount available — a share of a rushed collapse beats a polite share of nothing.

- Consider defecting one season early (second-to-last round) only if I expect the others to defect at the end anyway. This episode one boat did defect in season 5; defecting alongside them then would have netted a bit more, but the gain was small. The default is stay cooperative through the second-to-last round unless defection by others is already visible or the endgame grab is large.

- Note the endgame grab works best when the stock is near cap — which is exactly what cooperation buys me. Keep the stock healthy precisely so the final-season liquidation is worth more.

- General rule: keep me even with competitors in all middle rounds, harvest everything when the horizon ends. My total is what's scored, not the stock I leave behind.

1.text:
**Playbook for shared-stock fishery games**

- On the first season, I submit the stated sustainable share (or just under it). This signals cooperation and tests whether others do the same.

- If the posted history shows all boats landing at or below the sustainable share and the stock holding steady, I keep matching the sustainable share every season. Cooperation held perfectly through season 4 in my run; do not defect early — an early overcatch risks triggering retaliation and collapse for many remaining seasons.

- I watch the history each season for two things: whether anyone has defected, and whether the stock is dropping. If another boat overcatches but the stock stays near max, I stay cooperative rather than retaliating — one defection doesn't justify abandoning a stable arrangement.

- In the second-to-last season, defect with a modest overcatch (roughly 30–40% above the sustainable share, e.g. 15 vs. 11.1). This worked: I gained ~4 fish and the stock only fell to ~94, leaving the final season nearly intact. Others did not visibly retaliate in response.

- In the final season, there is no future to protect, so I take more than the sustainable share — but only modestly more (a few units above the share). A huge grab gains little if catches are limited by remaining stock or diminishing returns; a moderate overcatch is the safer default. Note the final-season sustainable share drops slightly if I overcaught the season before — the endgame defections still netted positive, so keep them.

- Never defect in an early or middle season when others are cooperating. The cooperative equilibrium held for the whole mid-game at ~11/boat; the only extra points came from endgame defections, which cost almost nothing.

- If the stock ever drops sharply or someone defects early, I reassess: defect in kind to avoid being exploited, but keep catches moderate so the stock survives to the last season.

- General rule: compute total expected fish across remaining seasons, not per-season greed. Protecting the stock dominates until there are ≤2 seasons left.

- Check the endgame timing carefully: with N seasons, the defection window is seasons N-1 and N only. Confirm from the header how many seasons remain before submitting.

2.text:
When the season prompt is put to me, I first check the current stock and the stated sustainable share, and I check the history of what the other boats actually landed.

While stock is at or near its cap and others are landing at the sustainable level, I submit exactly the sustainable share each season. This keeps the stock at max and preserves future seasons. In the episode this worked for five straight seasons: my restraint cost nothing because the stock stayed at 100.

If others overfish once, I do not panic-defect immediately; a single defection only dropped the stock from 100 to 94, which was still healthy. Match the quota again next season and watch whether it repeats.

If another boat overfishes in the second-to-last season, that is a signal it will fish hard in the last season too. In the final season I should not just take "a third" — I should take as large a catch as I plausibly can, since a greedy rival will take theirs regardless and leftover stock is pure waste to me.

On the final season, when no future remains, conservation has zero value: submit the largest catch I can, not the sustainable share and not a token bump. My final take of 31.4 was in the right direction; go bigger next time.

Do not be a pure sucker: if another boat takes above quota repeatedly, I take my revenge in kind while the stock still supports it, rather than subsidizing their overfishing with my restraint. My score is only my own landed fish, so once cooperation cannot be enforced, per-season I maximize my own catch, not group totals.

Note the timing asymmetry: a defection by a rival late in the game is more dangerous to me than an early one, because I have fewer seasons to earn back the loss. From season 5 onward, if a rival overfishes, consider raising my own catch the very next season rather than waiting for the final round.

Keep replies brief and always end with the required bracketed token.
